question.text: An elevator begins moving upward from a stationary state, with its acceleration changing over time as shown in the given graph. The acceleration is 2 ms⁻² between t = 0 and t = 4 s, remains 0 from t = 4 s to t = 8 s, and is −2 ms⁻² between t = 8 s and t = 12 s. Determine the total vertical displacement of the elevator from its initial level by the time it stops.
conditions: starts from rest (initial velocity is zero)
acceleration a = 2 ms⁻² for 0 ≤ t ≤ 4 s
acceleration a = 0 for 4 s < t ≤ 8 s
acceleration a = −2 ms⁻² for 8 s < t ≤ 12 s

figure.description: An acceleration-time graph showing acceleration a in ms⁻² on the vertical axis and time t in s on the horizontal axis. A horizontal line segment extends from t = 0 to t = 4 s at a = 2 ms⁻². The curve lies on the time axis (a = 0) from t = 4 s to t = 8 s. A horizontal line segment extends from t = 8 s to t = 12 s at a = −2 ms⁻².

solution.approach: Read the acceleration in each of the three time segments, find the velocity at each segment boundary, and add the distance covered in each segment.

steps.text: From t = 0 to 4 s, acceleration is 2 ms⁻² from rest. Find the velocity and distance covered by the end of this segment.
From t = 4 to 8 s, acceleration is 0, so the lift moves at the constant velocity 8 ms⁻¹. Find the distance covered.
From t = 8 to 12 s, acceleration is −2 ms⁻². Check that the lift comes to rest exactly at t = 12 s.
Find the distance covered while the velocity falls from 8 ms⁻¹ to 0 over this last segment.
Add the three distances to get the total height above the starting point.

common_mistakes.text: Treating zero acceleration in the middle segment as zero velocity, so skipping the 32 m travelled at constant speed and adding only the first and last segments: 16 + 16 = 32 m.
